skills.name: Reading about cash-crop production and marketing

note.text: A process account explains stages in a suitable order. Production concerns growing and preparing a crop; marketing concerns finding buyers and arranging a sale; transport connects locations. Sequence words such as first, then and finally help readers follow the account. A language lesson can explain these relationships without supplying agricultural treatment instructions or invented prices. Conditions differ by crop, season and place, so the passage is an original simplified example.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: Original passage: In an imaginary cocoa-growing community, growers prepare their produce and check its condition. They arrange transport to a collection point, where a buyer discusses quality and sale terms. The growers record the transaction and compare receipts with costs. A sale produces revenue, but transport and other costs affect what remains. The passage supplies no real market price or crop-treatment recipe.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Identify the main process and underline sequence signals. Distinguish a step from its purpose. When summarising, preserve both production and selling rather than reducing the process to receiving money. Do not add pesticide instructions or unverified statistics to the passage.
